solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Face pressure entering a cult

indicators.note: one letter going into the phrase it follows, so it sits inside

parts.note: a cult is a sect, a small religious group
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Pressure forcing its way into a cult, as a recruit might feel.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is one side or face of a matter, as in 'every face of the problem'.

clue.text: OK Sauce regularly put on mushroom with food

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter

parts.note: a cep is a porcini mushroom
table can mean the food served, as in 'keeps a good table'

explanation.surface: Seems to be a menu note approving sauce poured on a mushroom dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of Sauce, A and C.
explanation.definitionFit: OK means satisfactory or tolerable, so it is a synonym of passable.

clue.text: Stop cutting wavy hair each day

indicators.note: cutting into something splits it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a perm is hair set in waves or curls
to die is to stop, as an engine does

explanation.surface: An instruction to quit trimming someone's curly hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Per diem is Latin for 'by the day', meaning daily, as with an allowance.

clue.text: Singer's stake in church service

definitions.note: the 's is 'is', the link to the wordplay

indicators.note: in puts the stake inside the other two pieces

parts.note: use means service, as in 'of use'
an ante is a stake put up in poker

explanation.surface: A singer's investment in a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A chanteuse is a female nightclub vocalist, from the French word for a woman who sings.

clue.text: I connected — perhaps

parts.note: the words are what a telephone exchange worker might say after putting a caller through

explanation.surface: A short boast or confession that someone made a link.
explanation.walkthrough: In the days of manual telephone exchanges, the person at the switchboard connected callers, so 'I connected' is something they could truthfully claim; 'perhaps' flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A switchboard worker linked callers on old telephone exchanges, so 'I connected' describes their job.

clue.text: Artist in cartoon strip, oddly off-putting type

indicators.note: in places the artist inside the jumbled letters
oddly means strangely, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a standard abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: A cartoonist drawing a comic strip, odd and unnerving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' scrambles CARTOON STRIP and RA goes inside. 'off-putting' means putting things off, not unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps delaying tasks puts them off, so they are a habitual delayer.

clue.text: Wine and port given German approval

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a port, often shortened to Rio
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: Wine and port both getting a German nod of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink, fitting beside wine, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a Spanish red wine from the La Rioja region.

clue.text: Old Germans sent out at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Ancient Germanic warriors dispatched on a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Teutons were an ancient Germanic tribe; the word now denotes Germanic peoples generally.

clue.text: Dirty game starts to deteriorate

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: the starts of a word are its opening letters, here the first two

explanation.surface: A grubby match beginning to go downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby Union, RU, is a British ball game; 'starts' takes the opening pair of letters of deteriorate.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude can mean vulgar or smutty, as in a rude joke, a synonym of dirty.

clue.text: Light-headed female on bed I explored friskily

indicators.note: friskily means playfully and boisterously, so the letters are tossed about

explanation.surface: A tipsy woman exploring the bed playfully, a racy scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light-headed' suggests dizzy, but here it means having bleached, light-coloured hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with hair bleached chemically pale has a light-coloured head of hair.

clue.text: Remains in vehicle outside?

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a case is an outer covering, the outside of something

explanation.surface: A question about what is left in a car parked outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' looks like an instruction to put one piece round another, but it is simply a noun meaning a casing.
explanation.definitionFit: A carcase (also spelt carcass) is a dead body, the remains of an animal.

clue.text: Pompous, old and fat

parts.note: rotund means plump or fat

explanation.surface: A description of some portly, self-important elderly gent.
explanation.definitionFit: Orotund speech is pompous and inflated in style, synonym for grandiloquent.

clue.text: Left out, now play guitar on "Rocky" musical

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, shaken up, so the remaining letters are jumbled
out says the letter for the word left goes missing from the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A instruction to a band: sit this one out, now strum along to the song 'Rocky'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes L (Left) from NOW PLAY GUITAR ON, and 'Rocky' scrambles the remaining fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint Your Wagon is a Lerner and Loewe stage show, later a film, an example of a musical.

clue.text: Great. Put the flags out

definitions.meaning: famous or renowned, as in a great writer
marked an occasion joyfully, as by hanging bunting

explanation.definitionFit: The word means famous, like a renowned singer, and also the past tense of marking an event with festivities.

clue.text: They supply our occupying forces

indicators.note: to occupy is to fill a space, so one piece fills the inside of the other

parts.note: armies are military forces

explanation.surface: Someone noting who keeps our occupation troops equipped.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic in a mild way: these places supply weapons, so 'They supply' stands for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenals store and issue weapons, so they are the places that supply arms to troops.

clue.text: Group of actors close to stage

parts.note: the actors in a play are its cast

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A troupe of players standing near the front of the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, a group within a society.

clue.text: Party snack — fruit in soft drink, thanks

indicators.note: in places the fruit inside the drink

parts.note: cola is a soft drink
a hip is the fruit of the rose
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A party offering of fruit floating in a fizzy drink, with gratitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A small thin sausage often served on sticks at parties is a classic British buffet snack.

clue.text: Drunk, he's able to move supply

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk
the pronoun is taken as written; the 's is the link 'is'

explanation.surface: A drunk man who can still stagger along with the provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' here is the adverb from supple, not the noun or verb meaning provisions.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means supple and agile, describing a body that moves with easy flexibility.

clue.text: Piece of land or vehicle on it?

parts.note: a tract is an expanse of land

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether the thing is a field or the machine working it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the piece of land, so the definition is a vehicle found on a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm machine for pulling ploughs is driven across fields, so it is a vehicle on land.

clue.text: Murder sounds good to me in lift

indicators.note: in places the phrase before it within the word that follows

parts.note: to lift someone's spirits is to elate them
count me in, I'm in, is a way of saying a plan sounds good

explanation.surface: Someone casually agreeing to a killing proposed in an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' is not a homophone signal: the whole phrase 'sounds good to me' is the agreement I'M IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate a rival is a euphemism for killing them, so the verb fits murder.

clue.text: Song left for John Lennon?

parts.note: an air is a song or tune
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A song walking out on John Lennon, a Beatles reference.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool's airport is named Liverpool John Lennon Airport, so the Beatle's name serves as an example definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool's air terminal is named after the Beatle, so his name stands for it by example.

clue.text: One not suited for temporary work?

definitions.text: One not suited for temporary work?

parts.words: One not suited for temporary work?
parts.note: not suited reads as not wearing a suit, dressed informally, and temporary work is labouring hired by the day

explanation.surface: Seems to describe somebody unfit to take on a short-term job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not suited' pretends to mean unsuitable, but it means not wearing a suit, that is dressed casually.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker hired for odd jobs on a temporary basis does manual work without a regular contract.

clue.text: Place to learn about marriage

parts.note: uni, short for university, is a place of learning
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Seems to suggest a course where one studies wedlock.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage is a joining of two people, a wedding being their joining together.

clue.text: Dressed in rejected bridal clothing

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
in signals letters sitting inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone wearing a wedding outfit that was turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked an indicator for the hidden step; 'in' supplies it, while 'rejected' turns the run round.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad is an old past participle of clothe, meaning wearing clothes.

clue.text: European native about to conceal sex

indicators.note: concealing something hides it within, so the second piece goes inside
about here means turned round, so the word for native is written backwards

parts.note: natal means of one's birth, native
sex is Latin for six, which in Roman numerals is VI

explanation.surface: A local person on the point of hiding their gender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sex' is not gender here: it is the Latin word for six, written in Roman numerals. 'about' reverses the word for native before the numeral is tucked in.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Latvia, one of the Baltic states, is a European.

clue.text: Nuts for oats, more or less

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: Swapping nuts for oats, a muesli recipe adjusted roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done 'after a fashion' is achieved only roughly, an idiom meaning approximately.

clue.text: Lunatic called into action

indicators.note: into says the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: a deed is an action
rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: A madman summoned to take part in something.
explanation.definitionFit: Deranged means insane, the adjective sense of lunatic.

clue.text: Pallid old rocker, possibly a criminal

parts.note: wan means pale, pallid
a Ted, a Teddy boy, was a 1950s British rock and roll fan

explanation.surface: An ageing, pale rock musician who might be a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style suits who followed rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspect sought by police is on a poster saying the person is sought; a criminal may be so described.
